properties.name: Uttarapatha (Northern Highway / Grand Trunk Precursor)
properties.era: Vedic, Mauryan, Mughal to Modern (c. 1000 BCE – Present)
properties.connected_nodes: Taxila, Lahore, Kurukshetra, Indraprastha, Mathura, Kannauj, Prayagraj, Varanasi, Pataliputra, Champa, Tamralipti
properties.key_stations: Taxila, Lahore, Kurukshetra, Indraprastha, Mathura, Kannauj, Prayagraj, Varanasi, Pataliputra, Champa, Tamralipti
properties.commodities: Gandharan wool, silk bolts, lapis lazuli, fine horses, Bengal muslins, iron agricultural implements, imperial stone edicts
properties.chronicles: Megasthenes (Indica), Kautilya (Arthashastra), Xuanzang travels (630 CE), Sher Shah Suri (Sadak-e-Azam)
properties.historical_accounts: Megasthenes (Indica), Kautilya (Arthashastra), Xuanzang travels (630 CE), Sher Shah Suri (Sadak-e-Azam)
properties.significance: The great royal road of northern India connecting northwestern borderlands with the eastern seaport of Bengal, acting as the socio-economic and military spine of the Mauryan and Mughal empires.
properties.citation: Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) & Schwartzberg Historical Atlas

properties.name: Dakshinapatha (Great Southern Highway)
properties.era: Mauryan, Satavahana, & Chola Eras (c. 500 BCE – 14th c. CE)
properties.connected_nodes: Varanasi, Kaushambi, Vidisha, Ujjayini, Maheshwar (Narmada), Pratishthana (Paithan), Tagara, Amaravati, Kanchipuram, Madurai
properties.key_stations: Varanasi, Kaushambi, Vidisha, Ujjayini, Maheshwar (Narmada), Pratishthana (Paithan), Tagara, Amaravati, Kanchipuram, Madurai
properties.commodities: Black pepper, pearls from Gulf of Mannar, beryls from Coimbatore, fine cotton textiles, sandalwood, semi-precious carnelian beads
properties.chronicles: Kautilya (Arthashastra Book VII: 'Dakshinapatha is superior as it traverses mineral, diamond, and pearl country'), Periplus of the Erythraean Sea §50
properties.historical_accounts: Kautilya (Arthashastra Book VII), Periplus of the Erythraean Sea §50
properties.significance: The foremost trade artery connecting northern India to the rich mineral, gemstone, and textile emporia of peninsular India and the Satavahana capital at Paithan.
properties.citation: Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) & Ray, H.P. (Monastery and Guild)

properties.name: Central Caravan Route (Mathura–Vidisha–Ujjayini–Barygaza)
properties.era: Mauryan, Shunga, & Western Kshatrapa (c. 300 BCE – 400 CE)
properties.termini: Mathura / Vidisha ↔ Barygaza (Bharuch, Gulf of Khambhat)
properties.connected_nodes: Mathura, Gwalior, Vidisha (Heliodorus pillar), Ujjayini (Astronomical meridian), Mandu, Maheshwar, Barygaza
properties.key_stations: Mathura, Gwalior, Vidisha, Ujjayini, Mandu, Maheshwar, Barygaza
properties.commodities: Onyx, agate, chalcedony, spikenard, bdellium, cotton cloths, Roman gold coin imports, Mediterranean wine
properties.chronicles: Periplus of the Erythraean Sea §48 ('From Ozene all things useful for the country round are brought down to Barygaza')
properties.historical_accounts: Periplus of the Erythraean Sea §48, Ptolemy Geographia VII.1
properties.significance: Crucial trade artery funneling the agricultural and gemstone wealth of the Malwa plateau and northern plains directly into India's premier western Roman trading port.
properties.citation: Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) & Schoff, W.H.

properties.name: Western Indian Ocean Monsoon Maritime Route
properties.era: Ptolemaic, Roman, & Early Islamic Eras (c. 100 BCE – 12th c. CE)
properties.termini: Red Sea (Berenike & Myos Hormos) ↔ Barygaza, Muziris & Nelcynda
properties.connected_nodes: Alexandria, Berenike, Aden, Barygaza, Sopara, Kalyan, Muziris, Nelcynda, Quilon, Kanyakumari
properties.key_stations: Alexandria, Berenike, Aden, Barygaza, Sopara, Kalyan, Muziris, Nelcynda, Quilon, Kanyakumari
properties.commodities: Roman gold aurei, copper, tin, Italian amphorae wine, frankincense, Malabar black pepper ('Black Gold'), pearls, beryls, Chinese silk
properties.chronicles: Periplus of the Erythraean Sea, Pliny the Elder (Naturalis Historia 6.101: 'India drains our empire of 50 million sesterces annually')
properties.historical_accounts: Periplus of the Erythraean Sea, Pliny the Elder, Ptolemy Geographia
properties.significance: Exploitation of regular summer monsoon winds (Hippalus winds) allowed direct open-sea navigation between the Roman empire and Indian seaports in under 40 days.
properties.citation: Ministry of Culture (Project Mausam) & Casson, L. (Periplus Maris Erythraei)

properties.name: Bay of Bengal Maritime Network (Chola & Kalinga Route to Southeast Asia)
properties.era: Mauryan, Satavahana, Pallava, & Imperial Chola (c. 300 BCE – 13th c. CE)
properties.termini: Tamralipti, Arikamedu & Nagapattinam ↔ Suvarnabhumi (Kedah, Srivijaya & Malacca)
properties.connected_nodes: Tamralipti, Manikapatna, Machilipatnam, Arikamedu, Kaveripattinam, Nagapattinam, Andaman & Nicobar, Kedah (Kataha), Srivijaya (Sumatra), Canton
properties.key_stations: Tamralipti, Manikapatna, Machilipatnam, Arikamedu, Kaveripattinam, Nagapattinam, Andaman & Nicobar, Kedah, Srivijaya, Canton
properties.commodities: Bengal fine muslins, Coromandel painted chintz, iron weapons, camphor, cloves, nutmeg, sandalwood, Buddhist and Hindu iconography
properties.chronicles: Pattinappalai (Sangam text), Faxian travelogues (414 CE), Thanjavur Inscription of Rajendra Chola I (1025 CE naval campaign)
properties.historical_accounts: Thanjavur Big Temple epigraphs, Faxian, Chau Ju-Kua (Chu-fan-chi)
properties.significance: Maritime highway facilitating extensive commercial, religious, and architectural exchanges, giving birth to Indianized kingdoms and monumental temples across Southeast Asia.
properties.citation: Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) & Ministry of Culture (Project Mausam)

properties.name: Karakoram & Ladakh Silk Route Feeder
properties.era: Kushan, Tibetan, & Dogra Eras (c. 1st c. CE – 1949 CE)
properties.termini: Srinagar & Leh (Ladakh) ↔ Yarkand & Kashgar (Tarim Basin, Silk Road)
properties.connected_nodes: Srinagar, Kargil, Leh, Nubra Valley, Panamik, Karakoram Pass, Yarkand, Kashgar
properties.key_stations: Srinagar, Kargil, Leh, Nubra Valley, Panamik, Karakoram Pass, Yarkand, Kashgar
properties.commodities: Central Asian raw silk, jade from Khotan, pashmina (cashmere) wool, saffron, musk, tea, borax, silver yambus
properties.chronicles: Mirza Muhammad Haidar Dughlat (Tarikh-i-Rashidi), Sven Hedin (Transhimalaya), Survey of India trans-Himalayan surveys
properties.historical_accounts: Tarikh-i-Rashidi, Cunningham (Ladak: Physical, Statistical, and Historical 1854)
properties.significance: The highest commercial caravan route on Earth crossing five major passes above 5,000 meters, linking the Indian plains to the northern and southern Silk Roads of Central Asia.
properties.citation: UNESCO Silk Roads Programme & Cunningham, A. (1854)

properties.name: Gandhara–Khyber Silk Road Link (To Bactria)
properties.era: Achaemenid, Mauryan, Indo-Greek, & Kushan (c. 500 BCE – 8th c. CE)
properties.termini: Taxila & Peshawar ↔ Balkh (Bactra, Crossroads of Central Asian Silk Road)
properties.connected_nodes: Taxila, Peshawar (Purushapura), Khyber Pass, Nagarahara (Jalalabad), Kabul, Bamiyan, Balkh (Bactria)
properties.key_stations: Taxila, Peshawar, Khyber Pass, Nagarahara, Kabul, Bamiyan, Balkh
properties.commodities: Chinese raw silk, lapis lazuli from Badakhshan, Bactrian horses, Roman glassware, Greco-Buddhist sculptures, Sanskrit manuscripts
properties.chronicles: Xuanzang (Great Tang Records on the Western Regions 629 CE), Faxian, Strabo Geographica
properties.historical_accounts: Xuanzang, Strabo, Arrian Anabasis of Alexander
properties.significance: The definitive cultural and commercial corridor transmitting Buddhism, Indian mathematical concepts, and trade goods from India into Central Asia, China, and the Eurasian Silk Road.
properties.citation: UNESCO Silk Roads Programme & Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)

properties.name: Sikkim–Chumbi Valley Route (Old Silk / Tea Horse Branch)
properties.era: Pala, Tibetan, & British Raj (c. 8th c. CE – 1962 CE)
properties.connected_nodes: Calcutta, Siliguri, Kalimpong, Gangtok, Nathu La, Jelep La, Chumbi Valley, Gyantse, Lhasa
properties.key_stations: Siliguri, Kalimpong, Gangtok, Nathu La, Jelep La, Chumbi Valley, Gyantse, Lhasa
properties.commodities: Tibetan raw wool, musk, yak tails, medicinal herbs, Chinese tea bricks, Darjeeling tea, manufactured Indian cotton goods
properties.chronicles: Younghusband Expedition records (1904), Asiatic Society of Bengal memoirs, Survey of India frontier route logs
properties.historical_accounts: Younghusband (1904), Bell, Sir Charles (Tibet: Past & Present 1924)
properties.significance: The eastern Himalayan gateway between India and Tibet, handling over 70% of trans-Himalayan commerce until the mid-20th century.
properties.citation: Survey of India Archives & Asiatic Society of Bengal

properties.name: Malabar Coast 'Black Gold' Pepper Route
properties.era: Classical Antiquity to Early Modern (c. 300 BCE – 18th c. CE)
properties.connected_nodes: Honnavar, Mangalore, Cannanore, Calicut, Muziris, Cochin, Nelcynda, Quilon, Kanyakumari
properties.key_stations: Honnavar, Mangalore, Cannanore, Calicut, Muziris, Cochin, Nelcynda, Quilon, Kanyakumari
properties.commodities: Malabar Tellicherry black pepper, green cardamom, wild ginger, Malabar cinnamon, betel nut, Malabar teak for shipbuilding
properties.chronicles: Pliny the Elder, Periplus of the Erythraean Sea §56, Sangam Akananuru 149 ('Yavana ships arrive with gold and depart laden with pepper')
properties.historical_accounts: Sangam Akananuru, Pliny, Ibn Battuta (1342 CE), Vasco da Gama logs (1498 CE)
properties.significance: The epicentre of the global spice trade for two millennia, attracting Phoenician, Roman, Arab, Chinese, Venetian, and Portuguese fleets and dictating international geopolitical rivalries.
properties.citation: Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) & Kerala State Archaeology

properties.name: Coromandel Spice & Textile Coastal Route
properties.era: Sangam, Pallava, Chola, & Colonial (c. 200 BCE – 18th c. CE)
properties.connected_nodes: Pulicat, San Thome, Mamallapuram, Arikamedu, Poompuhar, Tranquebar, Nagapattinam, Korkai
properties.key_stations: Pulicat, San Thome, Mamallapuram, Arikamedu, Poompuhar, Tranquebar, Nagapattinam, Korkai
properties.commodities: Painted chintz textiles, dyed kalamkari cloth, natural indigo cakes, Ceylon cinnamon, Gulf of Mannar natural pearls, turtle shells
properties.chronicles: Pattinappalai, Periplus of the Erythraean Sea §60, Marco Polo (1292 CE description of the Pearl Fishery Coast)
properties.historical_accounts: Pattinappalai, Periplus, Marco Polo, VOC (Dutch East India Company) factory records
properties.significance: Coastal maritime corridor bartering world-famous south Indian textiles for Southeast Asian nutmeg, mace, and cloves, while commanding the celebrated pearl beds of Korkai.
properties.citation: Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) & Tamil Nadu Maritime History

properties.name: Lothal (World's Earliest Tidal Dockyard)
properties.era: Mature Harappan (c. 2400–1900 BCE)
properties.location_desc: Bhogavo River estuary, Gulf of Khambhat, Gujarat
properties.connected_nodes: Indus Valley cities (Mohenjo-daro, Harappa) ↔ Dilmun (Bahrain), Magan (Oman), Ur (Mesopotamia)
properties.commodities: Carnelian etched beads, worked ivory combs, copper ingots, steatite seals, shell bangles
properties.chronicles: Excavations by Dr. S.R. Rao (ASI 1955–1962), Mesopotamian cuneiform records of 'Meluhha' trade
properties.historical_accounts: ASI Excavation Memoir No. 78 (Rao, S.R. 1979/1985)
properties.significance: Features a trapezoidal kiln-burnt brick basin (214 × 36 m) with inlet and spillway lock gates engineered to float sea vessels during high tides, recognized as humanity's earliest known tidal dockyard.
properties.citation: Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) & UNESCO Tentative List

properties.name: Barygaza / Bharuch (Emporium of Western India)
properties.era: Mauryan, Satavahana, & Western Kshatrapa (c. 300 BCE – 400 CE)
properties.location_desc: Narmada River mouth, Gulf of Khambhat, Gujarat
properties.connected_nodes: Red Sea (Myos Hormos, Berenike) ↔ Ujjayini, Mathura, Pataliputra, Tagara, Paithan
properties.commodities: Exported spikenard, costus, bdellium, ivory, agate, carnelian, silks; Imported Italian wine, copper, tin, lead, gold & silver aurei
properties.chronicles: Periplus of the Erythraean Sea §41–49 ('The country of Barygaza is exceedingly fertile... the entrance is difficult on account of the tides')
properties.historical_accounts: Periplus Maris Erythraei, Ptolemy Geographia VII.1
properties.significance: The foremost western gateway for Indo-Roman commerce; pilot boats operated by the local king guided international merchant vessels safely through treacherous river mouth bores.
properties.citation: Archaeological Survey of India (ASI Vadodara Circle) & Schoff, W.H.

properties.name: Muziris / Pattanam (Roman Pepper Capital)
properties.era: Chera Kingdom & Roman Empire (c. 100 BCE – 6th c. CE)
properties.location_desc: Periyar River delta, Kodungallur / Pattanam, Kerala
properties.connected_nodes: Alexandria, Berenike ↔ Karur (Chera capital), Madurai, Nelcynda, Rome
properties.commodities: Exported Malabar black pepper, beryl gemstones, pearls, tortoise-shell; Imported Roman gold coin hoards, Terra Sigillata, amphorae
properties.chronicles: Periplus §53–54, Pliny Naturalis Historia 6.104, Tabula Peutingeriana (showing Temple of Augustus), Sangam Akananuru 149
properties.historical_accounts: Tabula Peutingeriana, Pliny, Sangam poetry, Muziris Papyrus (Vienna)
properties.significance: The greatest trading emporium of south India. The Muziris Papyrus documents a single 2nd-century Roman cargo ship (Hermapollon) carrying goods valued at over 131 talents of gold.
properties.citation: Kerala Council for Historical Research (KCHR) & Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)

properties.name: Arikamedu / Poduke (Roman Ceramic & Bead Port)
properties.era: Early Historic Indo-Roman (c. 200 BCE – 200 CE)
properties.connected_nodes: Mediterranean ports ↔ Suvarnabhumi, Kanchipuram, Kaveripattinam, Anuradhapura (Sri Lanka)
properties.commodities: Exported glass Indo-Pacific beads, fine cotton textiles, muslin; Imported Roman wine amphorae, Arretine ware ceramics, Roman intaglios
properties.chronicles: Periplus of the Erythraean Sea §60 (listing 'Poduke'), Excavations by Sir Mortimer Wheeler (1945)
properties.historical_accounts: Wheeler, R.E.M. (Ancient India No. 2, 1946), Casal, J.M. (1949)
properties.significance: Revealed extensive brick warehouse quays, dye-vats, and thousands of Mediterranean amphorae fragments, proving permanent settlement of Greco-Roman merchants on the Coromandel coast.
properties.citation: Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) & Wheeler, R.E.M.

properties.name: Tamralipti / Tamluk (Bay of Bengal Embarkation Port)
properties.era: Mauryan, Gupta, & Pala Eras (c. 400 BCE – 8th c. CE)
properties.location_desc: Rupnarayan River, Bengal Delta (Modern Tamluk, West Bengal)
properties.connected_nodes: Pataliputra, Varanasi, Taxila (via Uttarapatha) ↔ Sri Lanka, Kedah, Java, Sumatra, China
properties.commodities: Bengal fine muslins, terracotta plaques, iron tools, Buddhist manuscripts, spices from Southeast Asia, Chinese silk
properties.chronicles: Mahavamsa (Emperor Ashoka sending Bodhi tree sapling with Princess Sanghamitta), Faxian (411 CE), Xuanzang (639 CE), Yijing (673 CE)
properties.historical_accounts: Faxian (Record of Buddhistic Kingdoms), Xuanzang (Si-Yu-Ki), Yijing
properties.significance: The eastern maritime terminal of the ancient Uttarapatha highway where merchant fleets and Buddhist pilgrims boarded transoceanic vessels bound for Southeast Asia and China.
properties.citation: Archaeological Survey of India (ASI Kolkata Circle)

properties.name: Sopara / Shurparaka (Konkan Ashokan Port)
properties.era: Mauryan, Satavahana, to Silahara (c. 3rd c. BCE – 13th c. CE)
properties.connected_nodes: Arabia, Persian Gulf, Rome ↔ Paithan, Nashik, Junnar, Ujjain
properties.commodities: Exported cotton cloth, iron, timber, spices; Imported copper, Roman coins, Arabian incense
properties.chronicles: Mahabharata (sacred Shurparaka), Ashoka's Major Rock Edicts VIII and IX found here, Periplus §52, Ptolemy
properties.historical_accounts: Pandit Bhagwanlal Indraji (1882 excavations), Ashokan rock inscriptions
properties.significance: Ancient capital of the coastal province of Aparanta; 1882 excavations by Bhagwanlal Indraji un-earthed an Ashokan Buddhist stupa with a stone coffer containing sacred relic caskets.
properties.citation: Archaeological Survey of India (ASI Mumbai Circle)

properties.name: Poompuhar / Kaveripattinam (Chola Maritime Capital)
properties.era: Early Chola Sangam Era (c. 300 BCE – 500 CE)
properties.location_desc: Kaveri River confluence with Bay of Bengal, Tamil Nadu
properties.connected_nodes: Sri Lanka, Southeast Asia, Rome ↔ Uraiyur, Madurai, Thanjavur
properties.commodities: Pepper, pearls, precious coral, gemstones, horses from Arabia, manufactured silks from China
properties.chronicles: Sangam classics Silappadikaram and Manimekalai, Pattinappalai, Periplus §60, Ptolemy
properties.historical_accounts: Silappadikaram (Ilango Adigal), Pattinappalai (Kadiyalur Uruttirangannanar)
properties.significance: Celebrated in ancient Tamil epics; marine archaeological expeditions by the National Institute of Oceanography (NIO) discovered submerged brick structures, wharves, and ring-wells off its coast.
properties.citation: National Institute of Oceanography (NIO) & Tamil Nadu Archaeology Dept

properties.name: Korkai (Pandyan Pearl Fishery Capital)
properties.era: Early Pandyan Sangam Era (c. 4th c. BCE – 3rd c. CE)
properties.location_desc: Thamirabarani River estuary, Gulf of Mannar, Tamil Nadu
properties.connected_nodes: Rome, Alexandria, Sri Lanka ↔ Madurai (Pandyan capital)
properties.commodities: Natural Gulf of Mannar pearls, conch chanks, beryls, fine south Indian cottons
properties.chronicles: Periplus of the Erythraean Sea §59 ('Colchoi, where the pearl-fisheries are worked by condemned criminals'), Ptolemy Geographia VII.1
properties.historical_accounts: Periplus, Ptolemy, Sangam literature, Caldwell (1877 excavations)
properties.significance: The principal port and cradle of the Early Pandyan kingdom, famous throughout the ancient Greek, Roman, and Persian worlds as the world's finest pearl fishery center.
properties.citation: Tamil Nadu State Department of Archaeology & ASI

properties.name: Kalyan / Calliena (Satavahana Trade Port)
properties.era: Satavahana Dynasty (c. 2nd c. BCE – 3rd c. CE)
properties.location_desc: Ulhas River / Thane Creek confluence, Maharashtra
properties.connected_nodes: Red Sea, Persian Gulf ↔ Junnar, Paithan, Ter (via Nana Ghat mountain pass)
properties.commodities: Deccan black cotton cloth, iron weapons, timber, grain, Roman wines, bronze statues
properties.chronicles: Periplus §52 ('The city of Calliena, which in the time of the elder Saraganus became a lawful market-town')
properties.historical_accounts: Periplus of the Erythraean Sea §52, Nana Ghat rock inscriptions
properties.significance: Leading northern Konkan port connected to the Deccan interior via the Nana Ghat toll-gate pass; witnessed fierce naval and trade rivalry between the Satavahanas and Western Kshatrapas.
properties.citation: Archaeological Survey of India (ASI Western Circle)

properties.name: Nelcynda / Niranam (Ancient Malabar Pepper Mart)
properties.era: Early Historic Ay & Pandyan Era (c. 1st c. BCE – 3rd c. CE)
properties.location_desc: Pamba / Manimala River confluence, Niranam, Kerala
properties.connected_nodes: Rome, Alexandria ↔ Madurai, Kottayam, Western Ghats pepper hills
properties.commodities: Tellicherry black pepper, malabathrum (cinnamon leaves), tortoise-shell, Roman coins, fine Mediterranean pottery
properties.chronicles: Pliny the Elder (Naturalis Historia 6.26), Periplus of the Erythraean Sea §53–54 ('Nelcynda is distant from Muziris by river and sea about 500 stadia')
properties.historical_accounts: Pliny, Periplus, Ptolemy Geographia
properties.significance: Major pepper-exporting riverine port situated safely in the Kerala backwaters where Roman merchants sailed upriver on country rafts to load vast quantities of Malabar pepper.
properties.citation: Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) & Schoff, W.H.

properties.name: East India Company Gangetic Factory & Opium Corridor
properties.era: Colonial Era (c. 1757 – 1858 CE)
properties.connected_nodes: Calcutta, Hooghly, Murshidabad, Patna, Ghazipur, Varanasi, Mirzapur, Allahabad, Kanpur, Agra
properties.key_stations: Calcutta, Hooghly, Murshidabad, Patna, Ghazipur, Varanasi, Mirzapur, Allahabad, Kanpur, Agra
properties.commodities: Bihar manufactured opium (shipped to China in Opium trade), saltpetre (potassium nitrate for British gunpowder), raw Bengal silk, indigo dye, salt monopoly
properties.chronicles: East India Company Factory Records, Imperial Gazetteer of India, Trotter (The History of the British Empire in India)
properties.historical_accounts: EIC Factory Records, Hunter (The Imperial Gazetteer of India Vol. IV)
properties.significance: The principal economic extraction artery of the British East India Company along the Ganga, converting regional agrarian production into export revenues that funded imperial conquest.
properties.citation: National Archives of India & Imperial Gazetteer of India

properties.name: Bombay Hinterland Cotton & Opium Artery
properties.era: Colonial Era (c. 1850 – 1947 CE)
properties.termini: Nagpur & Berar Cotton Belt ↔ Bombay Port (Cotton Green)
properties.connected_nodes: Nagpur, Amravati, Akola, Khandesh, Jalgaon, Nashik, Thull Ghat, Kalyan, Bombay Port
properties.key_stations: Nagpur, Amravati, Akola, Khandesh, Jalgaon, Nashik, Thull Ghat, Kalyan, Bombay Port
properties.commodities: Raw baled Deccan cotton, Malwa opium, oilseeds, Bombay textile mill yarn, British Lancashire manufactured cloth imports
properties.chronicles: Bombay Presidency Gazetteer, Reports of the Cotton Commissioner of India (1868), Morris (The Emergence of an Industrial Labour Force in India)
properties.historical_accounts: Bombay Presidency Gazetteer Vol. IX, Cotton Supply Association Reports (Manchester 1862)
properties.significance: Fueled by the American Civil War (1861–1865) cotton famine, this corridor transformed Bombay into 'Cottonopolis', financed the city's Victorian public architecture, and accelerated modern banking and deep-water dock construction.
properties.citation: Maharashtra State Archives & Imperial Gazetteer of India

properties.name: Coromandel Calico & Indigo Corridor
properties.era: Colonial Era (c. 1639 – 1850 CE)
properties.termini: Fort St. George (Madras) ↔ Masulipatnam, Arcot & Salem
properties.connected_nodes: Masulipatnam, Guntur, Nellore, Pulicat, Fort St. George (Madras), Arcot, Kanchipuram, Cuddalore, Salem
properties.key_stations: Masulipatnam, Guntur, Nellore, Pulicat, Fort St. George (Madras), Arcot, Kanchipuram, Cuddalore, Salem
properties.commodities: Coromandel piecegoods (calicoes, muslins, longcloths), natural indigo dye cakes, saltpeter, British woolens
properties.chronicles: Madras Presidency Public Consultations, Love (Vestiges of Old Madras), Imperial Gazetteer of India
properties.historical_accounts: Vestiges of Old Madras (Love, H.D. 1913), Madras District Gazetteers
properties.significance: Anchored around the first territorial acquisition of the East India Company (Fort St. George, 1639), this corridor systematized procurement from village weaver guilds and funneled south Indian textiles to Europe and Southeast Asia.
properties.citation: Tamil Nadu Archives & Imperial Gazetteer of India

properties.name: Great Indian Peninsula Railway (GIPR, 1853 — Asia's First Line)
properties.era: Pioneering Railway Era (Inaugurated 16 April 1853)
properties.termini: Bombay (Bori Bunder / CSMT) ↔ Thane & Kalyan (Extended to Pune & Jabalpur)
properties.connected_nodes: Bori Bunder, Byculla, Dadar, Kurla, Bhandup, Thane, Kalyan Junction, Thal Ghat, Bhor Ghat, Pune
properties.key_stations: Bori Bunder, Byculla, Dadar, Kurla, Bhandup, Thane, Kalyan, Kasara, Igatpuri, Pune
properties.commodities: First passenger train in Asia (400 guests, 14 carriages, 21-gun salute, hauled by locomotives Sindh, Sultan & Sahib); raw cotton, postal mail, military troops
properties.chronicles: The Bombay Times (18 April 1853 report), Administrative Reports on Indian Railways (Public Works Dept), MacGeorge (Ways and Works in India 1894)
properties.historical_accounts: The Times of India archives (1853), GIPR Company minute books
properties.significance: Inaugurated the railway age across the Asian continent on Saturday, 16 April 1853 at 3:30 PM. Overcame the formidable natural barrier of the Western Ghats with pioneering reversing station incline viaducts.
properties.citation: National Rail Museum New Delhi & Indian Railways Heritage Directorate

properties.name: East Indian Railway (EIR, 1854 — Gangetic Coal & Trunk Line)
properties.era: Colonial Trunk Line Era (Inaugurated 15 August 1854)
properties.connected_nodes: Howrah, Serampore, Hooghly, Burdwan, Raniganj Coalfields, Asansol, Patna, Mughalsarai, Allahabad, Kanpur, Aligarh, Delhi Junction
properties.key_stations: Howrah, Serampore, Hooghly, Burdwan, Raniganj, Asansol, Patna, Mughalsarai, Allahabad, Kanpur, Delhi
properties.commodities: Raniganj bituminous coal (essential for steam engines & steamships), Gangetic foodgrains, jute, military personnel, millions of third-class passenger commuters
properties.chronicles: Bengal Hurkaru (16 Aug 1854), Huddleston (History of the East Indian Railway 1906), Government of India Railway Department Reports
properties.historical_accounts: Huddleston, G. (1906), East Indian Railway Committee Reports
properties.significance: Conceived by Rowland Macdonald Stephenson; opened on 15 August 1854. Connected the Bengal coalfields to Calcutta and Delhi, providing the industrial fuel and transport backbone of modern India.
properties.citation: National Rail Museum & Eastern Railway Heritage Archives

properties.name: Madras Railway (1856 — Peninsular East–West Trunk Line)
properties.era: Early Railway Era (Inaugurated 1 July 1856)
properties.termini: Royapuram (Madras) ↔ Walajah Road & Beypore (Calicut, Arabian Sea)
